items.title: Former CIA officer challenges secrecy over COVID origins records
items.summary: A retired CIA officer who helped review intelligence about the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic says he saw firsthand that reports being prepared for public release still showed what analysts concluded and why, even after details about intelligence sources and methods were removed. His sworn account, which a federal judge agreed to consider this week, challenges the government’s claim that it can release nothing more of substance from records sought by U.S. Right To Know. James E. Erdman III said in his declaration that intelligence reports about the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic were sent to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and other agencies to prepare them for public release. But aside from a single batch disclosed in June, he wrote, Erdman was unaware of any of the material becoming public. U.S. Right To Know submitted Erdman’s nine-page declaration on Nov. 17 in its lawsuit against ODNI over the disputed records that it requested three years ago under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The next day, U.S. District Court Judge David J. Novak allowed the nonprofit news group to file the declaration. Novak also accepted a supplemental brief and gave ODNI two weeks to reply. The agency’s motion to dismiss the case remains pending in the Eastern District of Virginia. The lawsuit seeks intelligence records on possible links between the Wuhan Institute of Virology (WIV) and the origins of COVID-19, including records involving the Chinese research…

Nearly two years after unauthorized drone activity prompted the closure of the airfield at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) in Ohio, newly released investigative records reveal additional details about the December 2024 incidents, including reports of synchronized drone maneuvers and communications disruptions experienced by military personnel. The documents, released by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on November 13, 2026, and received by The Black Vault on November 25, originated with the Air Force Office of Special Investigations (AFOSI). They detail three separate periods of reported drone activity between December 11 and 17, 2024, two of which were designated as FBI-led investigative matters. All three AFOSI investigative communications are marked closed. In each instance, the operators of the aircraft remained unidentified. items.title: FAA Releases Records on Major Northeast Air Traffic Control Outage, But Key Technical Details Remain Missing
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has released records documenting the September 21, 2026, air traffic control outage that disrupted operations at major airports across the northeastern United States, including Philadelphia, Newark, and New York-area airports. The records, obtained by The Black Vault through the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), include operational logs from Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON), national traffic management records, and facility metrics documenting the effects of the disruption. However, the November 17, 2026, response also identifies significant limitations in the records provided. Although the request specifically sought technical assessments, maintenance records, documentation of the equipment failures, and information concerning restoration efforts, the FAA stated that the Philadelphia ATCT/TRACON held no responsive records for several of those categories. The release provides an operational record of the outage and its effects on air traffic management, but does not include a final technical investigation establishing the sequence of equipment failures or the underlying causes. items.title: FAA Records Reveal Military Prepared to Engage Drone During San Diego Airport Shutdown; ATC Audio References Possible Shootdown
items.summary: A September 4, 2026, disruption at San Diego International Airport that delayed hundreds of flights is now documented in newly released Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) records, including air traffic control recordings and two Mandatory Occurrence Reports describing sightings of suspected drones near the airport’s runway. The records, obtained by The Black Vault through the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), provide additional details about what pilots and air traffic controllers reported during the incident, how flight operations were affected, and the involvement of law enforcement. They also reveal a previously unreported detail involving nearby Naval Air Station North Island, where military personnel reportedly were preparing to engage an unauthorized drone. More notably, an air traffic control recording contains a statement indicating that a drone near the military installation may have been shot down. While the FAA’s written report confirms that North Island personnel communicated their intention to engage an unauthorized drone, the separate reference to a possible shootdown remains unverified. No corroborating military records or public confirmation of such an engagement have been identified, as of the writing of this article. items.title: Jensen Huang is Back And He Has a Plan.
items.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and CEO, 11 days after the scandal that pushed him out, and the market answered in minutes: Nvidia went from the fourth most valuable company in the world to the second, added about a trillion dollars, and the US stock market added $3 trillion, about half of what it had lost in six weeks. items.title: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z)
items.summary: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are publishing final rules amending the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd- Frank Act) amended TILA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300 effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd- Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Consumer Leasing Act's threshold for exempt consumer leases, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Consumer Leasing Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

items.title: What Bitcoin Did
items.summary: Why the AI Bubble Is Designed to Pop | Whitney Webb & Mark Goodwin Investigative journalists Whitney Webb and Mark Goodwin join Danny Knowles to unpack the connections they trace between the Enron crash, the post-2001 national security state and today’s AI boom, and why a financial collapse could leave the people behind it even more powerful. Their argument is that we’ve seen this playbook before: use enormous amounts of debt to build infrastructure, leave investors and the public holding the losses, and consolidate ownership for pennies on the dollar when the bubble pops. Could AI become another massive transfer of wealth and power? We get into Enron’s hidden role in building modern internet infrastructure, Cantor Fitzgerald’s ties to Tether and stablecoins, Bitcoin miners pivoting to AI, and the battle to control the nuclear power, chips and data centers running it all. We also discuss the origins of Palantir and modern state surveillance, and why they reject the argument that America must sacrifice its freedoms to beat China. Can open-source AI deliver the freedom its supporters promise if the physical chokepoints underneath it remain in so few hands?
